sanskrit: citranyastamivāsīcca vastujātamaśobhi ca | sthagitā iva saṃvṛttāstatra cakradharādayaḥ || 5 || dakṣopi vadanaglānimavāpya saparicchadaḥ | punaryathākathaṃcicca yajñaṃ prāvartayandvijāḥ || 106 ||
english: 103-106. The sacred sacrificial objects and offerings were defiled by jackals and hounds. Cakoras and crows flew over the sacrificial pavilion. The sacrificial hall turned instantly into a cremation ground. Everything got stuck up in the place where it was. All objects became motionless as though painted in a picture and lacked lustre. Viṣṇu and others became awestruck and suspicious. Dakṣa and his attendants became pale-faced. The Brāhmaṇas then resumed the Yajña somehow.
